clue.text: Leave empty venue in which a mouser resides

indicators.note: in which says the following letters go inside the emptied venue
resides completes the picture of the cat living inside the venue's letters
empty means with the inside taken out, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: venue emptied of its middle leaves V and E
a mouser is a cat kept to catch mice

explanation.surface: Clear out of a deserted building where a cat has taken up residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty venue' leaves V and E, and 'in which ... resides' puts A CAT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a place is to leave it, giving up occupation of a room or seat.

clue.text: Certainly in the pink

definitions.meaning: a reply agreeing to a request
an idiom for being in fine health

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they are in excellent health.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: as a reply agreeing to something, and as a report on how you feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: saying yes to a request, and describing someone in excellent health.

clue.text: Have little effect — as would blunted skate?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for failing to impress or persuade
a blade with no edge would glide without scoring the rink

explanation.surface: A skater grumbles that dull blades get them nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an argument that makes no impression on the listener, like a blunt blade on a frozen pond.

clue.text: Before winner at the death, draw level

indicators.note: the draw word goes before the winner's last letter

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

indicators.note: at the death means at the very end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of winner is R

explanation.surface: Just before a late winner, a team scrapes a draw to draw level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the death' is sports slang for the final moments, here the last letter of 'winner'. 'level' looks like an adjective about the score; it is a noun, a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or layer, one of a series of rows placed one above another.

clue.text: Demonstration of arrogance in song a bit misplaced

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong places have to be rearranged into the right ones

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A singer's arrogance shows in a slightly off-key number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit misplaced' looks like a mild criticism of the song; 'a bit' is fodder and only 'misplaced' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragging loudly about your own achievements is the most obvious way pride shows itself.

clue.text: Just around the corner — as is setting sun?

definitions.meaning: where the sun sits at dusk, on the line between earth and sky

explanation.surface: Someone at dusk says the end of the day is near.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the phrase literally, which the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something imminent, borrowed from a ship or storm first seen far off where sky meets land.

clue.text: Fielder in error?

definitions.meaning: a cricket position close behind the batter, beside the wicketkeeper
a small careless mistake, a lapse

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder has dropped a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the slips are fielders stationed close behind the batter, beside the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a cricket position waiting for edged catches, and a small careless mistake.

clue.text: Bunch of flowers one takes off

parts.note: Roman numeral one
a plane taking off goes up

explanation.surface: A florist removes a bunch of blooms from display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' tempts as removal; here it is lift-off, as an aircraft climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a plural is needed because a bunch holds several stems of these purple garden blooms.

clue.text: Player in concert, leader of orchestra, look!

parts.note: a gig is a concert

indicators.note: whatever leads a word is at its front, so the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of ORCHESTRA
lo = look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A musician performing at a concert, with the orchestra's leader in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' looks musical in a clue about an orchestra, but it means a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a man who plays the field, kept by wealthy women for romance, is a player in that sense.

clue.text: Quite hot after temperature in back turns

indicators.note: the pair goes in the reversed back word
turns means turns round, so the back word is read in reverse

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: the hot letter comes after the temperature letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: It gets quite hot once the temperature rises and your back starts to turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes REAR into RAER, and 'in' sets T and H between its A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather is an adverb meaning quite or somewhat, as in rather warm.

clue.text: Remarkable man joins band, shortly

indicators.note: the man is attached to the end of the band's letters

parts.note: STRIP (band) without its last letter
a king is a chess man

explanation.surface: A notable musician is about to join a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' reads as a group of musicians; it is a strip. 'Man' is a chess piece, here the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something eye-catching and impressive enough to draw attention and comment.

clue.text: Unfortunately, free agents do procrastinate

indicators.note: things going badly for the letters means they end up disordered

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: A grumble that people left to themselves always put things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a link, but it is fodder: the three words together supply all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone reluctant to move walks slowly, scuffing along, so it means delaying deliberately.

clue.text: Logs cut, fine bark

parts.note: WOOD (logs) without its last letter
F = fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Firewood chopped, and the tree's rough bark is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' sits by logs as the tree's skin, but it is the dog's.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound a dog makes, written as a word in comics and children's books.

clue.text: Groom up for marriage, bride uncertain, all ending

indicators.note: every word contributes the letter at its end

parts.note: last letters of uP foR marriagE bridE uncertaiN

explanation.surface: A groom ready to wed while the bride has doubts, and everything ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' pretends to be the bridegroom; it is the verb, to tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds smooth their feathers with their beaks, and people fussing over their appearance do the same.

clue.text: Stagger as if drunk, gaze when falling back

indicators.note: a retreating word goes backwards, so read its letters right to left

parts.note: to leer is to gaze lewdly

explanation.surface: A drunk stares blearily and then topples backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling back' looks like part of the drunk's stagger; it tells you to turn the gaze round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lurch and sway unsteadily, as after a blow or too much wine.

clue.text: Sign initial on banknotes in Turkish currency

indicators.note: the initial goes in the currency word

parts.note: the lira is the currency of Turkey

indicators.note: initial on means the first letter appearing on the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of banknotes is B

explanation.surface: A sign printed on Turkish banknotes, in the national currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial on banknotes' gives B, which goes 'in' LIRA after LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is the seventh sign of the zodiac in astrology.

clue.text: From hiding place, shoot bird

definitions.meaning: to fire from cover at a target

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at a bird from a hide.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from the bird: it was so hard to hit that marksmen good enough were called snipers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a marsh wader with a long beak, and firing at people from concealment.

clue.text: Coming together, instruments clashing

parts.note: parts that lock come together
horns are brass instruments

explanation.surface: An orchestra's instruments join in a jarring discord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clashing' sounds like discordant music; it means fighting, like stags with antlers locked.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from rutting stags, whose antlers catch together as they fight, used for people in open conflict.

clue.text: South American in rave-up, dancing

indicators.note: dancers move about the floor, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: A South American is dancing at a lively party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link, but it supplies two of the fodder letters. A rave-up is a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a native of Lima or the Andes belongs to one country on that continent.

clue.text: Plane is not broken up for scrap

parts.note: a jet is a jet-engined plane

indicators.note: broken up means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft that isn't broken up gets sent off for scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' rearranges IS NOT into TISON. 'Plane' is the aircraft, not the tool or the flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard or throw away something unwanted, to scrap it.

clue.text: Is man on battlefield drawing on literary work?

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it here, so the battlefield comes first

parts.note: the front is where battle is fought
used as printed
a chess man is a piece

explanation.surface: A soldier at war sketches while drawing on his reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing on' pretends to mean 'using'; 'drawing' is a picture and the whole phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The illustration printed facing a book's title page, a picture placed at the front of a volume.

clue.text: Next post filled by company

indicators.note: something filled has another thing put inside it, so company goes in

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
Co. = company

explanation.surface: A job vacancy about to be filled by a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job; it is the verb, to dispatch a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: following immediately in order, as the runner-up after the winner.

clue.text: Correct site working

parts.note: a site is a spot
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a website so it works again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' reads as a verb, to fix; it is the adjective. The answer is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for exactly right, as a dart landing precisely on its target point.

clue.text: Show hosted by Essex politician

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the answer is held inside the next words

parts.note: essEX POlitician

explanation.surface: A trade fair is staged by a local MP in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; here its letters matter only for the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for exposition: a large public exhibition, such as a world's fair or trade fair.

clue.text: Dundonian, for example, backs a Home Counties town

indicators.note: something that backs another stands behind it, so it comes after

parts.note: used as printed
someone from Dundee, a city in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scotsman supports an English commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' reads as supports; here it puts the Scotsman behind A. The Home Counties are the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Berkshire town famous for its royal racecourse, in a county bordering London.

clue.text: Bet placed, nothing originally pocketed …

indicators.note: pocketed means taken into a pocket, so the letter is held inside the placed word

parts.note: put means placed, set down

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of nothing is taken

parts.note: the first letter of nothing is N

explanation.surface: A wager was laid, but nothing came of it at first and the money was pocketed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives N from 'nothing', and 'pocketed' puts it inside PUT. A punt is British slang for a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is an informal British term for a bet or a speculative gamble.

clue.text: Picture in bedroom lifted up

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting letters reads them bottom to top
the answer lies inside the following words

parts.note: bedrooM LIFted

explanation.surface: A painting in the bedroom has been hung higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' does double duty: its letters are in the hidden run, and it is part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a motion picture, and people still say they are going to the pictures.

clue.text: Head of mammoth in particular on a mammoth!

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it
the head of a word is its top, which in a down entry is the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of MAMMOTH
e.g. = for example, in particular
used as printed

explanation.surface: Someone points out the head of a woolly mammoth.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'mammoth' twice on purpose: first as the animal whose initial is used, then as the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for enormous, from the Greek for great, as in a blockbuster success.

clue.text: … and I bet differently after nothing acquired!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the nothing letter

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: differently means in another way, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Following on from the punt, I bet a different way and got something for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the betting picture on from the clue before. 'differently' rearranges AND I BET into BTAINED, which comes 'after' O.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get or acquire it, so obtained means acquired.

clue.text: Einstein I observed in rank below family

indicators.note: the letter is seen within the rank's name, so it goes inside

parts.note: in biology, genus is the rank below family
used as printed

explanation.surface: Einstein studying biological classification.
explanation.walkthrough: In taxonomy the ranks run family, then genus, then species.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's name is used as a common noun for anyone of exceptional intellect.

clue.text: Terrific explosive

explanation.surface: Praise for something thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, but each is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: Nobel's blasting stick, and slang praise for something sensational.

clue.text: Rule about ammunition ultimately for big gun

indicators.note: the rule word goes about, around, the final letter

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle, as in church law

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of ammunition is taken

parts.note: the last letter of ammunition is N

explanation.surface: A regulation on ammunition decides the fate of a heavy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives N, and 'about' wraps CANON round it to double the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy gun, the classic artillery piece.
